status: draft written at step 0 from facts that were checked against the board's guide, its data and the ForgeKernel documentation; task targethw completes it (the development machine's measured values, the final wording).
role: The GPU every submission is graded on. Nothing measured anywhere else is the score: when a reading taken on another machine disagrees with this file, this file is right.

arch_notes.cubin_portability: An sm_100a cubin does not run on a CC 10.3 device, nor does an sm_103a cubin run here: there is no forward compatibility between the two.
arch_notes.family_conditional: sm_100f is the only target whose cubin runs on both CC 10.0 and CC 10.3.

tensor_throughput.sfu_note: special-function units, the instructions attention relies on (EX2 and the like)

software.basis: the board's open-source evaluation image. The board's live image may differ; a difference, once known, is recorded here.

protocol.address: a new address for the tensors on every call (random offset, a multiple of 256 B)
protocol.stopwatch: the CUPTI kernel span of one call: from the start of its first kernel to the end of its last. Host gaps between kernels count.
protocol.reading: the median of the timed calls
protocol.input_group: one group is drawn for the last round and only that group is timed

correctness: the output must be a torch.Tensor with the reference's shape and dtype
inf or NaN in the solution is wrong (only allow_negative_inf lets a -inf at the reference's position through)
an all-zero solution where the reference is non-zero is wrong
elementwise |solution - reference| <= atol + rtol * |reference|, with the tolerance the workload names

scoring.at_baseline: T_k = T_b scores 0.5; at T_SOL it scores 1.0
scoring.problem: the arithmetic mean of its workloads' S
scoring.t_b: the board's own optimized PyTorch baseline for the workload: a latency it measured once and froze, not something measured during an evaluation
scoring.t_sol: the board's speed-of-light time for the workload, computed by its SOLAR analysis ahead of time

evaluation.process: each solution is evaluated in a subprocess of its own under a hard time limit, and everything in it is compiled again: inline CUDA through torch.utils.cpp_extension, Triton and CuTe DSL just in time, torch.compile.

time_limits.basis: the defaults of the open-source evaluator; the board's live limits are not published

evaluation.review: the board checks for cheating with a validator and an LLM code review, and marks a submission it disqualifies.

submission.form: one file, submission.py, with a top-level run(*args)
submission.arguments: positional only, in the order the problem defines: the inputs, then the pre-allocated outputs (destination-passing style). Argument names are not enforced; the order and the count are.
submission.outputs: pre-allocated by the evaluator: write the result into them
languages: PyTorch operators (cuBLAS, cuDNN, SDPA, torch._scaled_mm, torch.compile)
CUDA C++ inline in the .py, compiled at run time through torch.utils.cpp_extension
submission.not_importable_note: to use their code, embed the source in the submission and keep its license
submission.compile_target: CUDA C++ is compiled for sm_100a unless the submission names its own -gencode / -arch; Triton and CuTe DSL compile for the device that runs them
submission.collection: a track submission is one archive with a directory per kernel, named exactly as the kernel, each holding its submission.py; only .py is accepted there, and a kernel that is missing scores 0
prohibited: launching hidden CUDA streams outside the measured path
starting background threads during the evaluation
returning a lazy proxy instead of a concrete tensor
producing degenerate output (NaN, inf, all zeros) that does not match the reference
submission.prohibited_consequence: a workload that fails correctness or is rejected scores 0; a submission caught cheating is disqualified and the score is lost

dev_machine_may_differ.difference: Compute capability. The target is CC 10.0 (sm_100a); the development machine is a B300, CC 10.3 (sm_103a).
dev_machine_may_differ.effect: A cubin built for one does not run on the other, in either direction; only sm_100f runs on both.
dev_machine_may_differ.what_to_do: Never name an architecture in the code: build the compile options from the device's compute capability at run time. Before a submission is exported, check that it compiles for the target without running it (Triton cross-compiled to sm_100a, inline CUDA compiled with -gencode arch=compute_100a,code=sm_100a).

dev_machine_may_differ.difference: SM count. The target has 148; the development machine has up to 160, depending on the model (not yet measured).
dev_machine_may_differ.effect: A persistent kernel, a grid size or a wave count tuned on the development machine may not be the best on the target.
dev_machine_may_differ.what_to_do: Never hard-code the SM count: query it at run time. While developing, the environment variable FK_TARGET_SMS may say 148 so that a kernel lays its grid out for the target; on the board the variable does not exist and the kernel must fall back to the query.
dev_machine_may_differ.status: the target's count is measured; the development machine's is to be measured

dev_machine_may_differ.difference: Memory. 192 GB HBM3e on the target, 288 GB on the development machine; the bandwidth is the same 8 TB/s.
dev_machine_may_differ.effect: A kernel that fits a working set only on the development machine does not fit on the target.
dev_machine_may_differ.what_to_do: Size buffers for 192 GB, never for what the development machine happens to have.

dev_machine_may_differ.difference: Dense NVFP4 throughput. 10 PFLOPS on the target, 15 on the development machine (1.5x).
dev_machine_may_differ.effect: A kernel bound by dense FP4 throughput looks faster on the development machine than it will score: the local estimate is optimistic.
dev_machine_may_differ.what_to_do: Treat the local score of such a kernel as an upper bound and let the board's result decide; record the ratio of local estimate to board result per problem.

dev_machine_may_differ.difference: SFU throughput. 5 TeraExp/s on the target, 10.7 on the development machine (about 2x).
dev_machine_may_differ.effect: A kernel heavy in softmax or other transcendental work looks faster on the development machine: the local estimate is optimistic.
dev_machine_may_differ.what_to_do: Treat the local score of such a kernel as an upper bound and let the board's result decide; record the ratio of local estimate to board result per problem.

dev_machine_may_differ.difference: Clocks. The target is locked at 1500 MHz (SM) and 3996 MHz (memory). The development machine should be locked the same way; whether it can be is not yet measured.
dev_machine_may_differ.effect: Different clocks change the balance between compute and bandwidth, so the best tile for one may not be the best for the other.
dev_machine_may_differ.what_to_do: Lock the development machine to the target's clocks before measuring; when they cannot be locked, record the clocks that held with every reading.
dev_machine_may_differ.status: the target's clocks are verified; the development machine's lock is to be measured

dev_machine_may_differ.difference: Software. The evaluation image is CUDA 13.1.1, Python 3.12, torch 2.9.0, fbtriton 3.7.1, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.4.2. Whether that stack compiles and runs on CC 10.3 is not yet measured, and the board's live image may differ from the open-source one.
dev_machine_may_differ.effect: If the board's Triton does not support sm_103, kernels can only be developed with another Triton, and what that Triton compiles is not what the board runs.
dev_machine_may_differ.what_to_do: Measure it on the development machine first; keep the development environment as close to the evaluation image as it can be; record every difference here.
dev_machine_may_differ.status: the image's versions are verified; their behaviour on CC 10.3 and the board's live image are unknown

dev_machine_may_differ.difference: Readings. Every reading taken on the development machine is a development reading (dev-only); the board's is the score.
dev_machine_may_differ.effect: The two can differ by more than the FP4 and SFU effects above.
dev_machine_may_differ.what_to_do: Compare a development reading with the board's result for the same submission where possible, and record the ratio per problem.

rules: The kernel is graded on an NVIDIA B200 (CC 10.0, sm_100a, 148 SMs, 8 TB/s) with its clocks locked at 1500 / 3996 MHz and the L2 cache cold on every call. That GPU, not the one you run on, is what you optimize for.
Do not use any feature that CC 10.0 lacks. Never name an architecture in the code: derive it from the device at run time.
Never hard-code the SM count: query it. FK_TARGET_SMS overrides it when it is set, and it is not set on the board.
Dense FP4 throughput and SFU throughput are higher on the development GPU: the timings of kernels bound by them are optimistic there.
The submission is one submission.py with a top-level run(*args); the arguments are positional (inputs, then pre-allocated outputs).

Allowed libraries: PyTorch operators, Triton, CuTe DSL, cuBLAS / cuDNN through torch, CUTLASS headers; CUDA C++ only inline, compiled at run time through torch.utils.cpp_extension. Everything else must be embedded as source.
Leave global state as you found it: restore any torch.backends flag you change inside run() before it returns.

The L2 cache is flushed before every timed call, and the inputs are cloned and land at a new address on every call. Never rely on cache residency across calls or on pointer identity. Minimise the bytes you move; fuse what would otherwise be separate kernels.
The stopwatch is the span from the first to the last kernel of one call: host-side gaps between kernels count. Keep the Python between launches minimal, or launch everything from one kernel.
Outputs are pre-allocated: write into them directly; do not allocate a result and copy it over.
The kernel must compute the problem's function for every legal input within the tolerance. Nothing may depend on particular input values or on how the evaluator behaves.

Every evaluation compiles from scratch: keep the cold start (import and all compilation) well inside a minute. A candidate whose cold start exceeds 100 seconds is not exported. Prefer a table of per-shape constants over run-time autotuning, and cache nothing outside the process.
